BiblicalUsage: Anath is known only as the father of Shamgar, the judge who killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad. Judges names him twice, both times to place Shamgar, and says nothing more about the man himself.
TheologicalSignificance: A name with no story of its own still matters, because God remembers the father behind the deliverer, and Shamgar's victory is tied to a real family, not a legend.
